_comment: Source of truth for Wren's App Store listing in its primary language.
Every other locale is translated from this file, so edit it here and
re-run the push rather than editing anything in App Store Connect by hand.
Apple's limits: name 30, subtitle 30, promotionalText 170, keywords 100,
description 4000. The push script checks all of them before sending.
Shared fields — name and the two URLs — come from common.json.
subtitle: Places, kept in Apple Maps
promotionalText: Screenshot the places people tell you about. Wren reads the names, finds them, and puts them straight into a guide in Apple Maps.
description:
Someone sends you a reel. Five places you have to eat at in Rome, a rooftop bar in Lisbon, a bookshop down an alley in Tokyo. You watch it, you mean to remember, and by Thursday it is gone.

Wren catches them.

Screenshot the places as they appear. Wren reads the names off the screen, works out which places they actually are, and drops the lot into a guide in Apple Maps — where you will be standing when you need them.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Screenshot what you see. From a reel, a post, a message from a friend, or a photographed page of a guidebook.

2. Wren reads the names. Text recognition runs on your phone, so your screenshots never leave it. Wren also reads the caption to work out which city you are looking at, and asks you to confirm.

3. Check the list. Every place shows what was read next to what was matched, so a wrong match is obvious. Anything not found — or found wrongly — can be searched again by hand.

4. Straight into Apple Maps. Not a copy of your places in another app. An actual guide, in the Maps you already use.

ANYWHERE, NOT JUST RESTAURANTS

Restaurants and bars, certainly. Also viewpoints, markets, hotels, galleries, shops, trailheads, beaches and the odd petrol station someone insists does the best coffee for fifty miles. Anywhere with a name and a location.

LISTS FROM ELSEWHERE

Places do not have to come from a screenshot. Wren also reads a list exported from another app — CSV, KML, KMZ, GPX, GeoJSON, or a Google Takeout export of your saved places — and looks each one up the same way, using the coordinates in the file to aim the search.

NO ACCOUNT, NO TRACKING, NOTHING COLLECTED

Wren has no sign-in and collects nothing about you. Your screenshots are read on your device and are never uploaded. The only thing that leaves your phone is the name of a place, sent to Apple Maps to find it — exactly as the Maps app does.

Wren does not connect to Instagram or any other service, and reads nothing from your accounts. It only reads screenshots you choose to give it.

FREE, WITH ONE OPTIONAL PURCHASE

Guides of up to three places are free, for good. Two things are a single one-time purchase: saving a guide with more than three places, and adding to a guide you already have. No subscription, nothing that renews, and it restores on your other devices at no further cost.

ADDING TO A GUIDE YOU ALREADY HAVE

Share a guide from Apple Maps, paste the link into Wren, and Wren reads the places already in it. Newly found places sit alongside them, and one guide is made holding both.

Worth knowing what Apple allows here. Maps offers no way to add to a guide that already exists, so the result is a new guide holding everything, which you keep instead of the old one. Wren keeps the places afterwards, so the guide can be made again if anything goes wrong. A single place is the exception — send it on its own and Maps itself will offer to add it to a guide.

reviewNotes:
Wren is free for guides of up to three places. TWO things require a one-time
non-consumable purchase: (1) saving a guide with more than three places, and
(2) adding to a guide the user already has in Apple Maps. The complimentary
code below unlocks both.

TO TEST THE PAID FEATURES WITHOUT PURCHASING: long-press the "Wren" title in
the top-left of the main screen, then enter this code:

    7QFG-7FVY-QXP6-2AT6

This entry point exists for App Review and for people the developer has given a
complimentary code to. It is not advertised anywhere in the app and is not
reachable by ordinary users. Codes are issued individually and checked against a
server, so a code cannot be shared onward. This code is not single-use and will
keep working across resubmissions.

Entering a code is the only time Wren contacts a server of its own. It sends the
code and a random identifier for the device, nothing else. Everything the app
does otherwise happens on the device.

TO TEST THE APP, tap "Add" at the bottom left. It offers three sources:

1. "Add screenshots" — take or save a few screenshots containing place names
   (for example a screenshot of a social post listing restaurants in a city) and
   select them. Wren reads the names on device using the Vision framework, asks
   which city they are in, and finds them using MapKit. Tapping "Make a guide"
   opens Apple Maps with the places in a new guide.

2. "From a file" — opens the document picker and reads a list exported from
   another app: CSV, KML, KMZ, GPX, GeoJSON, or a Google Takeout export. Each row
   is looked up with MapKit, aimed at the coordinate in the file where there is
   one. A sample CSV is two lines, e.g.
       name,latitude,longitude
       Padella,51.5054,-0.0903

3. "From an existing guide" — paste a link to an Apple Maps guide, which Maps
   produces via Share then Copy Link. Wren decodes the places already in it and
   shows them as a collapsed group. This is the second paid feature, so it will
   ask for the purchase unless the code above has been entered.

On point 3, please note: Apple Maps offers no way to add places to a guide that
already exists, so publishing produces a NEW guide holding the old places and
the new ones together. This is stated in the app before publishing, and in the
App Store description. It is a limitation of the Maps guide link format, not an
attempt to duplicate the user's data.

Wren requires no account and no sign-in.
